There are two types of hemoglobin in human blood: oxyhemoglobin and deoxyhemoglobin. The two types of hemoglobins absorb different amounts of light at different wavelengths. Pulsation of human arteries can cause changes in the blood flow, leading to changes in the light absorption amount. However, the light absorption amount of non-blood tissues (skin, muscles, and bones) is generally considered to be constant. Therefore, SpO₂ can be obtained by measuring changes in the light absorption amount caused by blood volume fluctuations.
